verdict.rationale: Airbyte is primarily a UI-driven platform, but its docs say the Terraform provider lets you "automate and version control your Airbyte configuration as code." PyAirbyte offers a Python code path, the API allows programmatic control alongside orchestrators like Airflow, and Connector Builder sits on a low-code YAML format. Code-first versioning therefore depends on add-on tooling (Terraform, PyAirbyte) layered over a UI/server-centric product, and portability rests on self-hosting the open-source Core. Missing for 10: native repo-first pipeline definitions as the primary workflow, documentation of review/CI workflows for pipeline config, and independent or hands-on corroboration of the Terraform/PyAirbyte code-as-config experience.
